previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, recurrent urinary tract infections, and urinary retention requiring an indwelling catheter, was admitted for treatment of a positive urine culture with multidrug-resistant organisms, including Pseudomonas. Although largely asymptomatic, due to his immunocompromised state and prior urosepsis, the infectious disease team recommended a five-day course of IV meropenem to eradicate potential colonizing bacteria. The Foley catheter was removed upon admission, and the patient successfully voided without difficulty. A prostate ultrasound showed no abscess. Repeat urine culture after treatment showed no growth. The patient was discharged on a regimen of weekly fosfomycin for long-term suppression and instructed to monitor for urinary symptoms. He remained stable throughout the admission with no complications.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS)
Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter

HISTORY:  ___ man status post liver transplant with history of
cervical spinal fusion and difficulty swallowing.  EGD performed this morning
with question of erosion of posterior esophagus from anterior cervical fusion
hardware.  Evaluation for leakage of contrast.

COMPARISON:  None.

SINGLE-CONTRAST ESOPHAGRAM:  This exam was performed with difficulty secondary
to the patient's inability to stand and limited mobility.  

The patient was given several swallows of water-soluble contrast to evaluate
the cervical esophagus in the AP and lateral projections.  Although the
inferior aspect of the cervical esophagus is somewhat obscured in the captured
spot images of the lateral projection due to overlying shadows from the
shoulders, real-time fluoroscopy demonstrates contrast flowing past the area
of prior anterior cervical spinal fusion hardware with no evidence of residual
contrast collection or leakage of contrast outside of the esophagus.

The esophagus is seen in close apposition to the surgical hardware on the
lateral view, but in the AP projection it appears slightly deviated to the
left and therefore it is difficult to determine if the esophagus actually
abuts the surgical hardware; nonetheless it appears very close fluoroscopy.

Additional real-time fluoroscopy of the area after several swallows
demonstrates no residual contrast in the esophagus or in the area surrounding
the anterior cervical fusion plate.

Residual contrast was seen in the vallecula and some laryngeal penetration was
also noted, however there was no gross aspiration during this exam.

The patient proceeded to have his neck CT immediately after this examination.

IMPRESSION:  

1.  No evidence of leakage of contrast from the esophagus.  

2.  No evidence of esophageal diverticula.  

3.  Close apposition of the esophagus to the anterior cervical fusion plate
with normal passage of contrast past this area. No unexplained
collection/accumulation of the ingested water-soluble contrast after
swallowing.

4.  Residual contrast in the vallecula and some penetration with no evidence
of gross aspiration of contrast.

screws are again seen.

IMPRESSION:  Bowel gas pattern consistent with ileus with no evidence of
obstruction.

There is no pelvicalyceal dilation and the kidneys concentrates and excretes

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, a guidewire was
advanced through the indwelling left arm PICC line, and subsequently into the

peel-away sheath was then placed over the guidewire.  A new single-lumen PICC
line measuring 45 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath
with its tip positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of
the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.
The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated fluoroscopically guided PICC line exchange for a
new 4 ___ PICC line.  Final internal length is 45 cm, with the tip
positioned in the SVC.  The line is ready to use.

PERCUTANEOUS ___ GASTROJEJUNAL FEEDING TUBE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  ___ male with history of liver transplant, now presenting
with esophageal erosions and malnutrition.  Today, the patient comes in for
placement of an enteral feeding tube.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___, ___ fellow, Dr. ___, ___ attending,
and Dr. ___, ___ attending, who were present and supervising throughout
the whole procedure.

ANESTHESIA:

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of a total of
250 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed.  During this time, patient's
hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.

Local anesthesia was also provided with 1% lidocaine.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:

A written informed consent was obtained after explaining the procedure,
benefits, risks and alternatives involved.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The upper abdomen
was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure timeout
was performed as per ___ protocol.

Given our inability to perform nasogastric intubation we had originally
planned to perform a primary percutaneous jejenostomy.
A scout image of the abdomen was obtained, which in fact demonstrated a
moderately dilated stomach and surrounding small bowel loops. A limited cone
beam CT was performed confirming anterior position of the stomach. We decided
to form a percutaneous gastric access with a view to placing a gastrojejunal
feeding tube.

Under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance and following administration of 1%
lidocaine, three T-tack gastropexy sutures were subsequently deployed,
approximating the stomach to the anterior abdominal wall in a triangular
fashion.  Intra gastric position was confirmed with aspiration of air and
injection of small amount of contrast.  A small incision was made between the
T-tack buttons and an 18 gauge needle was introduced into the stomach under
fluoroscopic guidance.  The position of the needle was confirmed to be
intragastric with small amount of contrast injection.  An 0.035 ___ wire
was coiled within the stomach.  The needle was removed over the wire and soft
tissue tract was dilated.  A 5 ___ sheath was then advanced over the wire. 
Using a 5 ___ Kumpe catheter and an 035 glidewire, the wire and catheter
were advanced into the duodenum and into the proximal jejunum.  The ___
wire was exchanged for a stiff Amplatz wire and following facial dilatations,
a 14 ___ peel-away sheath was advanced.  A 14 ___ ___ tube was
placed over the wire with its tip positioned in the proximal jejunum. The
guidewire was removed and retaining loop of the catheter was formed in the
duodenum and locked after confirming position of the catheter by contrast
injection.  The catheter was subsequently flushed, capped, and secured to the
skin with a Flexi-Trak.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:
Given the moderate dilatation of the stomach on cone beam CT, we elected to
perform direct percutaneous gastric access and place a gastrojejunal feeding
tube rather than attempt a ___ percutaneous jejunal feeding tube .

Uncomplicated placement of a 14 ___ gastrojejunal tube under fluoroscopic
guidance.  
The tip lies in the proximal jejunum.
